group.passage: Next month, our city will try something new: on the first Sunday morning of every month, Main Street will be closed to cars and opened to people on foot and on bikes. Before the plan begins, the city asked residents for their views, and some of their comments are shown below.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Laura
passage_parts.text: My two boys have been begging for years to ride their bikes somewhere wider and safer than our narrow lane. A whole morning on an empty Main Street sounds like a dream to them, and honestly, to me as well.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Mr. Brooks
passage_parts.text: Most of the people who buy flowers at my shop on Main Street drive in from nearby towns on Sunday mornings. Without them, I could barely make ends meet, so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.

passage_parts.label: C
passage_parts.title: Olivia
passage_parts.text: If the city closed Main Street every weekend, I would be the first to complain. But once a month? Drivers can surely take another road for one morning so that everyone else can enjoy a quieter town.

passage_parts.label: D
passage_parts.title: Mr. Harris
passage_parts.text: I have lived above the bakery on Main Street for forty years, and the trucks are usually too loud for me to hear my radio. Once they are gone, I will carry a chair outside and spend a peaceful hour listening to the birds.

passage_parts.label: E
passage_parts.title: Victor
passage_parts.text: The bus I drive normally stops right outside the market. On car-free Sundays, I will have to drop my riders off near the train station instead, fifteen minutes away on foot, and some of them are over eighty. Is one quiet morning really worth that?

passage_parts.label: F
passage_parts.title: Megan
passage_parts.text: Some shop owners say a street without cars means a street without customers, but I welcome the change. People on foot stop to look in windows, and tired shoppers buy coffee, which is just what I sell.

passage_parts.label: G
passage_parts.title: Andy
passage_parts.text: Every Sunday I drive my mother, who can no longer walk far, to her favorite breakfast shop on Main Street. She could never manage three blocks from the nearest parking lot, so I can’t support a plan that forgets people like her.

passage_parts.label: H
passage_parts.title: Jenny
passage_parts.text: Our school band has wanted to play in public for months, and the middle of Main Street would make a perfect stage. We have already asked the city whether we can perform on the first car-free Sunday.

questions.stem:
下列簡短敘述摘記上方留言的重點。請從文章中找出兩個單詞（word），分別填入下列句子空格中，並視句型結構需要做適當的字形變化，使句子語意完整、語法正確，並符合全文文意。每格限填一個單詞（word）。（填充，4分）
The comments show that residents are divided over the plan. One critic worries about elderly passengers being [[1]] off at a stop far from the market, while some supporters look forward to a little [[2]] and quiet.

tags.key_phrase: drop my riders off near the train station → elderly passengers being dropped off at a stop far from the market

questions.stem:
下列簡短敘述摘記上方留言的重點。請從文章中找出兩個單詞（word），分別填入下列句子空格中，並視句型結構需要做適當的字形變化，使句子語意完整、語法正確，並符合全文文意。每格限填一個單詞（word）。（填充，4分）
The comments show that residents are divided over the plan. One critic worries about elderly passengers being [[1]] off at a stop far from the market, while some supporters look forward to a little [[2]] and quiet.

questions.stem:
From (A) to (H) in the comments above, which ONES are against the plan?
請選出留言者前的英文大寫字母，並劃記在答題卷作答區內。（多選題，4分）
Which phrase in the comments means “to have just enough money to pay for the things you need”?（簡答題，2分）

1.explanation_zh: 摘要句說有一位反對者擔心年長乘客「在離市場很遠的站被放下車」。開公車的 Victor 說，無車的星期日他得把乘客載到火車站附近就讓他們下車（drop my riders off），走路還要十五分鐘，有些乘客已經超過八十歲。being ___ off 是被動的動名詞（being + 過去分詞），drop 的過去分詞要重複字尾 p 再加 -ed，寫成 dropped；drop someone off＝讓某人下車。
evidence: On car-free Sundays, I will have to drop my riders off near the train station instead, fifteen minutes away on foot, and some of them are over eighty.
The bus I drive normally stops right outside the market.
1.strategy_zh: 先看語法：being 後面接過去分詞，表示「被…」；再看語意：elderly passengers 對應「over eighty」的乘客，at a stop far from the market 對應「平常停在市場門口、改停火車站附近、走路十五分鐘」。找到後把 drop 改成過去分詞，注意拼法。
hints: being 後面要接過去分詞（被動）。
找一則提到「年長的乘客」與「市場」的留言，看他說會怎麼讓乘客下車。
留言裡是 drop my riders off，請寫出 drop 的過去分詞（注意要重複字尾）。

2.explanation_zh: 住在主街麵包店樓上的 Harris 先生說，卡車平常吵到他聽不見收音機，封街那天他要搬張椅子到外面，聽著鳥叫度過「平靜的」一小時（a peaceful hour）；Olivia 也期待一個比較安靜的小鎮。摘要句 a little ___ and quiet 的空格要不可數名詞，把形容詞 peaceful 轉成名詞 peace，peace and quiet 是「清靜、安寧」的固定說法。peacefulness 也是 peaceful 的名詞形、語法語意都通，一併接受。
evidence: Once they are gone, I will carry a chair outside and spend a peaceful hour listening to the birds.
I have lived above the bakery on Main Street for forty years, and the trucks are usually too loud for me to hear my radio.
Drivers can surely take another road for one morning so that everyone else can enjoy a quieter town.
2.strategy_zh: a little 後面接不可數名詞，___ and quiet 是一組並列的名詞；先想 peace and quiet 這個常用搭配，再回到支持者的留言找它的來源字：形容詞 peaceful 去掉 -ful 就是名詞。
hints: a little 後面、and quiet 前面要填不可數名詞。
找一則支持者的留言：平常卡車很吵，封街那天他想怎麼度過一小時？
留言用的是形容詞 peaceful，請改成名詞（___ and quiet 是常用搭配）。

3.explanation_zh: (B) Brooks 先生說星期日的客人多半從鄰近城鎮開車來，沒有他們他幾乎無法維持收支，所以堅決反對（firmly against）。(G) Andy 的媽媽走不遠，沒辦法從三條街外的停車場走到早餐店，所以他無法支持（can’t support）這個計畫。(E) Victor 沒有直接說「反對」，但他說無車日公車只能停在離市場步行十五分鐘的火車站附近，乘客有人超過八十歲，最後反問「一個安靜的早上真的值得嗎？」，意思是不值得，態度是反對（要推論）。(C) Olivia 的 if 條件句講的是「如果每個週末都封街」這個假設情況（與事實相反），她對一個月一次的計畫是支持的。(A) Laura、(D) Harris 先生、(F) Megan、(H) Jenny 都期待或歡迎無車日，不是反對者。
evidence: Without them, I could barely make ends meet, so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
She could never manage three blocks from the nearest parking lot, so I can’t support a plan that forgets people like her.
On car-free Sundays, I will have to drop my riders off near the train station instead, fifteen minutes away on foot, and some of them are over eighty.
Is one quiet morning really worth that?
If the city closed Main Street every weekend, I would be the first to complain.
Drivers can surely take another road for one morning so that everyone else can enjoy a quieter town.

option_notes_zh.A: Laura 說一整個早上在空蕩蕩的主街騎車，對孩子和她自己都像夢想一樣，是支持。
option_notes_zh.C: if 條件句講的是「每個週末都封街」的假設（與事實相反），Olivia 對一個月一次的封街是支持的，認為駕駛繞路一個早上就好。條件句容易讓人誤選。
option_notes_zh.D: Harris 先生期待卡車不在時搬張椅子到外面、聽鳥叫度過平靜的一小時，是支持。
option_notes_zh.F: Megan 提到有些店家認為沒車就沒客人，但她自己歡迎這個改變（I welcome the change），是支持。
option_notes_zh.H: Jenny 的樂團想在主街中央表演，已經向市政府申請第一個無車日的演出，是支持。

3.strategy_zh: 態度分類題：逐則判斷「支持／反對」，並找出表態的那一句。注意兩件事：(1) if 條件句講的如果是假設的別種情況，要看說話者對「實際計畫」的結論；(2) 沒有直接說 against 的留言，要從反問句或描述的後果推論態度。提到反方說法（Some shop owners say…）的人，不一定就是反對者。
hints: 逐則留言判斷：對每月一次的無車日是支持還是反對？
有一則留言沒有直接說反對，但用一個反問句表達態度。
Olivia 的 if 條件句講的是哪一種情況？她對一個月一次的封街怎麼看？

A: A whole morning on an empty Main Street sounds like a dream to them, and honestly, to me as well.
B: Without them, I could barely make ends meet, so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
C: If the city closed Main Street every weekend, I would be the first to complain.
Drivers can surely take another road for one morning so that everyone else can enjoy a quieter town.
D: Once they are gone, I will carry a chair outside and spend a peaceful hour listening to the birds.
E: On car-free Sundays, I will have to drop my riders off near the train station instead, fifteen minutes away on foot, and some of them are over eighty.
Is one quiet morning really worth that?
F: Some shop owners say a street without cars means a street without customers, but I welcome the change.
G: She could never manage three blocks from the nearest parking lot, so I can’t support a plan that forgets people like her.
H: Our school band has wanted to play in public for months, and the middle of Main Street would make a perfect stage.
We have already asked the city whether we can perform on the first car-free Sunday.

4.explanation_zh: make ends meet 是「收支平衡、勉強維持生計」，也就是錢剛好夠支付生活所需。Brooks 先生說，如果沒有那些開車來買花的客人，他幾乎無法維持收支（could barely make ends meet）。
evidence: Without them, I could barely make ends meet, so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
4.strategy_zh: 定義題：先把英文定義換成中文「錢剛好夠用、維持收支」，再找哪一則留言在談生意和收入；答案只寫三個字的片語，不要把 barely 或 could 一起抄。
hints: 定義以 to 開頭，要找動詞片語。
找一則擔心少了客人、生意會受影響的留言。
答案是三個字，第一個字是 make。

translation_zh.text:
下個月起，我們的城市要嘗試一件新鮮事：每個月第一個星期日的早上，主街將禁止汽車通行，開放給步行和騎腳踏車的人。計畫開始之前，市政府詢問了居民的看法，以下是部分留言。

A（Laura）我的兩個兒子好幾年來一直吵著要找個比我們家窄巷更寬、更安全的地方騎腳踏車。在空蕩蕩的主街上騎一整個早上，對他們來說就像美夢成真；老實說，對我也是。

B（Brooks 先生）到我主街花店買花的人，大多是星期日早上從鄰近城鎮開車過來的。沒有他們，我幾乎無法維持收支，所以任何讓他們的車進不來的計畫，我都堅決反對。

C（Olivia）如果市政府每個週末都封閉主街，我會第一個抱怨。但一個月一次？駕駛人一個早上繞別條路當然沒問題，這樣其他人就能享受一個比較安靜的小鎮。

D（Harris 先生）我住在主街麵包店樓上四十年了，平常卡車吵到我連收音機都聽不見。等卡車不在了，我要搬張椅子到外面，聽著鳥叫，度過平靜的一小時。

E（Victor）我開的公車平常就停在市場門口。到了無車的星期日，我只能讓乘客在火車站附近下車，走路要十五分鐘，而且有些乘客已經超過八十歲了。一個安靜的早上真的值得這樣嗎？

F（Megan）有些店家說，沒有車的街道就是沒有客人的街道，但我歡迎這個改變。走路的人會停下來看櫥窗，走累了的購物者會買咖啡，而咖啡正是我賣的東西。

G（Andy）每個星期日，我都開車載已經走不遠的媽媽去主街上她最喜歡的早餐店。她絕對沒辦法從最近的停車場走三條街過去，所以我無法支持一個忘了像她這樣的人的計畫。

H（Jenny）我們學校的樂隊好幾個月來一直想找機會公開演出，主街正中央會是完美的舞台。我們已經向市政府詢問，能不能在第一個無車的星期日表演。

evidence: On car-free Sundays, I will have to drop my riders off near the train station instead, fifteen minutes away on foot, and some of them are over eighty.
1.explanation_zh: 批評者是公車司機 Victor，擔心年長乘客要在離市場很遠的火車站下車；文中 drop ... off，被動式 being 後接過去分詞 dropped。

evidence: Once they are gone, I will carry a chair outside and spend a peaceful hour listening to the birds.
2.explanation_zh: 支持者（如 Mr. Harris）期待安靜時光；a little 後需名詞，與 quiet 構成固定搭配 peace and quiet，由文中 peaceful 改為名詞 peace。

evidence: Without them, I could barely make ends meet, so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
Is one quiet morning really worth that?
She could never manage three blocks from the nearest parking lot, so I can’t support a plan that forgets people like her.
3.explanation_zh: 反對者：花店老闆 Mr. Brooks 明言 firmly against；公車司機 Victor 以反問質疑值不值得；Andy 說 can't support。Olivia 只反對每週封街、接受每月一次，其餘 Laura、Mr. Harris、Megan、Jenny 皆支持。

B: Without them, I could barely make ends meet, so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
E: Is one quiet morning really worth that?
On car-free Sundays, I will have to drop my riders off near the train station instead, fifteen minutes away on foot, and some of them are over eighty.
G: She could never manage three blocks from the nearest parking lot, so I can’t support a plan that forgets people like her.

evidence: Without them, I could barely make ends meet, so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
4.explanation_zh: make ends meet 意為收支勉強平衡、錢剛好夠支付所需，符合題目定義；Mr. Brooks 說沒有開車來的顧客就難以維持生計。

evidence: On car-free Sundays, I will have to drop my riders off near the train station instead, fifteen minutes away on foot, and some of them are over eighty.
1.explanation_zh: 摘要句是 elderly passengers being ___ off at a stop far from the market，對應 Victor 說的 drop my riders off near the train station；被動語態 being 後要接過去分詞，所以 drop 要改成 dropped。

evidence: Once they are gone, I will carry a chair outside and spend a peaceful hour listening to the birds.
2.explanation_zh: a little ___ and quiet 是慣用語 peace and quiet；文中 Mr. Harris 提到想要安靜的一小時（a peaceful hour），peaceful 要轉成名詞 peace。

evidence: so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
Is one quiet morning really worth that?
so I can’t support a plan that forgets people like her.
3.explanation_zh: Mr. Brooks 明說 firmly against，Victor 用反問質疑為了一個安靜早晨讓高齡乘客多走路是否值得，Andy 說不能支持這個忽略行動不便者的計畫；其餘 A、C、D、F、H 都表示支持或期待。

B: so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
E: Is one quiet morning really worth that?
G: so I can’t support a plan that forgets people like her.

evidence: Without them, I could barely make ends meet, so I am firmly against any plan that keeps their cars away.
4.explanation_zh: make ends meet 的意思就是收入剛好夠付基本開銷，Mr. Brooks 說沒有開車來買花的客人，他勉強才能維持生計。

A.evidence: A whole morning on an empty Main Street sounds like a dream to them, and honestly, to me as well.
A.explanation_zh: Laura 說在空蕩蕩的主街騎一整個早上，對兩個兒子和她自己都像美夢，是期待、支持無車日，不是反對者（ST）。

C.evidence: Drivers can surely take another road for one morning so that everyone else can enjoy a quieter town.
C.explanation_zh: 前一句的 if 條件句講的是「每個週末都封街」這個與事實相反的假設；對實際的每月一次封街，Olivia 認為駕駛繞路一個早上就好，讓大家享受較安靜的小鎮，是支持（ST*）。

D.evidence: Once they are gone, I will carry a chair outside and spend a peaceful hour listening to the birds.
D.explanation_zh: Harris 先生期待卡車不在時搬椅子到外面聽鳥叫、享受平靜的一小時，是歡迎無車日，不是反對（ST）。

F.evidence: Some shop owners say a street without cars means a street without customers, but I welcome the change.
F.explanation_zh: 「沒車就沒客人」是 Megan 轉述其他店家的說法，她自己用 but 轉折後明說 I welcome the change，而且認為行人會帶來咖啡生意，是支持（ST）。

H.evidence: We have already asked the city whether we can perform on the first car-free Sunday.
H.explanation_zh: Jenny 的樂團把主街中央當成理想舞台，已經向市政府申請在第一個無車日演出，是期待這個計畫，不是反對（ST）。
